title: Artificial beaver dams saw juvenile coho salmon survival rates go from 8% to 60%
summary: This article describes how artificial beaver dams constructed in California streams dramatically improved juvenile coho salmon survival rates from just 8% to 60%, providing crucial habitat and protection for the endangered fish species during their critical early life stage.
problem_solved: It addresses the critically low survival rates of juvenile coho salmon due to habitat loss and degraded stream conditions in California.
why_valuable: This demonstrates an effective, low-cost ecological restoration technique that could help recover endangered salmon populations without expensive infrastructure.
